### Summary

Suppose someone adds an entry to `constraint-dependencies` due to some bug in an indirect dependency. Then, they upgrade to a new version of the direct dependency which removes that indirect dependency, or remove the direct dependency entirely. Doing so won't remove the `constraint-dependencies` entry. If nobody notices it, it is possible this `constraint-dependencies` entry may linger long after it has ceased to serve any purpose.

What if there was a setting like `require-use-dependencies = true`, which would trigger an error if an individual constraint in `constraint-dependencies` (or `build-constraint-dependencies` or `override-dependencies`) wasn't actually used? That would mean, when you removed the indirect dependency, `uv lock` would fail?

Or maybe this is more like a lint rule for `uv check` (if that did more than just run `ty`)? Or for `ruff check` (if you were to add uv-specific lint rules)?
